- tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py:1188-1189 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test asserts _decide("for i in a b; do gh api --help; done") is None (no decision), but the issue explicitly requires bare help to be "treat[ed] like any other read in the whole-command decision" and CLAUDE.md §23.H (as updated by this PR's own diff) says "A complete `for VAR in TOKEN…; do BODY; done` over literal IDs is also approved when every item is a vetted `gh api` read". The new sentence added to the §23.H read row states bare help "is a read too", so a literal loop whose body is only `gh api --help` (i.e. every item is a vetted read) should resolve to allow, not no-decision. The implementation adds KIND_READ for bare help in the per-invocation loop (template line 1503-1505) but the literal-loop approval path (_is_approvable_read_loop) does not classify bare help as a vetted read, so the whole command falls through.
  WHY: A literal loop like `for i in a b; do gh api --help; done` would still require a permission prompt in Auto mode (no decision -> allow-list/Auto-mode classifier decides) even though the issue and the new CLAUDE.md prose say it should be treated like any other read and approved like other literal read loops.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:1106-1124; `tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py:1185-1186` | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The literal-loop body validator does not recognize bare `gh api --help` as a valid read body item. `_is_loop_gh_api_read(["--help"])` calls `parse_gh_api_args(["--help"])` at line 1114, which raises `Unreadable("unknown gh api flag \`--help\`")` because `--help` is not in `_BOOL_FLAGS` (line 174) or `_VALUE_FLAGS` (line 155). The `except Unreadable` at line 1115 catches it and returns `False`. The bare-help shortcut at lines 1503-1505 bypasses `parse_gh_api_args` for the main invocation classification, but the loop body validator does not have the same bypass.
  WHY: The command `for i in a b; do gh api --help; done` gets no decision (None) instead of allow. The test `test_literal_loop_over_bare_help_gets_no_decision` at line 1185 asserts `is None`, which matches the current behavior but violates the issue contract. The issue says "Treat the call like any other read in the whole-command decision, including the safe-helper pipe rules." CLAUDE.md §23.H says "A complete `for VAR in TOKEN…; do BODY; done` over literal IDs is also approved when every item is a vetted `gh api` read." Since bare help is now classified as KIND_READ, a literal loop over bare-help reads should be approved. The fix is to make `_is_loop_gh_api_read` recognize bare help, e.g. by adding `if _is_bare_gh_api_help(args): return True` before the `parse_gh_api_args` call, and update the test to assert `allow`.
- Requirement: The issue requires the new code in `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` to take effect in this repository, the new tests in `tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py` to pass, and the parity contract between the live `.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` and the template to hold. The issue's delivery constraint says "Deliver it twin-first... The master session copies the file into .claude/ in a [claude-twin-sync] commit."
  Expected change site: `.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` must be a byte-identical copy of `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py`. The template has the three #6668 hunks (docstring lines 26-27, `_BARE_HELP_ARGS` / `_is_bare_gh_api_help` at lines 179-189, invocation-loop shortcut at lines 1503-1505); the live copy lacks them.
  Evidence of absence: The PR changed files list includes only the template copy. The live copy `.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` does not contain `_BARE_HELP_ARGS` or `_is_bare_gh_api_help` (verified by grep). CI fails: `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` → `test_live_copies_match_their_templates` reports "Live .claude/ copies differ from workflow-templates/.claude/ for: hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py". The new tests load `GUARD_PATH` at `tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py:27` (the live copy), which lacks the bare-help shortcut, so they cannot pass. The delivery constraint defers the live sync to the master session, but the PR is opened in a state where CI is red and the merge gates (ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS includes `lint`) refuse auto-merge. The interactive behaviour the issue asked to fix is unchanged in this repository until the `[claude-twin-sync]` commit lands.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
